notes: Real Internet Archive scan (Lewis Carroll, 'Alice's Adventures in Wonderland', John Tenniel illustrations, ca. 1910 reprint edition, IA identifier alicesadventures0000lewi_i4x4) trimmed to the 12 pages covering Chapter I's title/heading page ('ALICE IN WONDERLAND. CHAPTER I. DOWN THE RABBIT-HOLE.') through the White Rabbit, the locked hall, and the 'DRINK ME' bottle scene. Chosen as the positive case for defect F (dense first-person-quoted dialogue in ordinary book prose -- 'and what is the use of a book,' thought Alice, 'without pictures or conversations?' -- must never be misdetected as a code block) and defect E (the real chapter heading and the running header, which alternates every page between the chapter title 'DOWN THE RABBIT-HOLE.' and the book title 'ALICE IN WONDERLAND.' with an arabic folio, must survive extraction). This is a real halftone-era scan (slightly soft/uneven contrast, unlike a born-digital PDF), so the embedded OCR text layer itself has minor artifacts (e.g. 'ALICE iN WONDEPLAND'); ground truth here was transcribed by reading the pypdfium2 page renders at ~144 DPI directly, independent of that OCR layer. All 12 pages carry legible body prose, so phrase_recall_applies (pages<=12, expect=='ok', >=3 phrases/page) gates the 0.8 recall floor for this fixture. Public domain: Lewis Carroll died 1898, first published 1865; this particular printing is ca. 1910, itself over a century old, with no rights restriction recorded in Internet Archive's item metadata.
recall_exempt_reason: The embedded OCR text layer of this halftone-era scan is itself degraded (it systematically reads 'o' as 'e': 'nething te de', 'peeped inte the begk', 'cativersatiens'). Ground truth here is transcribed from the rendered page images per the corpus contract, so exact-phrase recall would measure the source scan's OCR quality rather than this extractor's fidelity.
